validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed — independent of GEM entirely. The wiki's own cited leads check out: jpt.spe.org (verified) and lywitness.com (Arabic, read) both describe Saipem's Aug-2023 ~$1bn EPC award covering 'laying 28km of pipelines to connect the DP3, DP4 and Sabratha platforms' plus a 5,000-t gas recovery module on DP4; mellitahog.ly is the operator's own site (context only, not cited). Independently, nsenergybusiness.com's project profile (verified, read in full) gives the precise two-segment breakdown that matches GEM's row split exactly: 'DP3 to DP4: a 14-inch cladded pipeline of 8.5km' (= sibling P6716) and 'DP4 to Sabratah to Onshore: Around 20km long 10-inch CS and a 4-inch CS pipelines... connect DP4 Platform to Sabratah Platform, then to Mellitah Onshore Plant' (= this row, P7617). That is a direct, specific match for Length=20km and Diameter='10,4in' (two parallel lines, 10in + 4in) — the automated screen flagged 'value not found' only because the source spells it as prose ('10-inch...and a 4-inch') rather than the compact GEM notation; on manual read it fully supports the recorded value. Fresh 2026 reporting (oilprice.com, libyaherald.com, both verified) independently re-confirms the '10-inch, 20km' line from Bouri/DP4 to Sabratha to Mellitah, so this is not just a 2023-era claim. Fuel=Gas and FuelSource='Bouri Field' are confirmed (attaqa.net, verified, read; matches all English coverage — associated/raw gas from the offshore Bouri field). CLASSIFICATION caveat: PipelineType='transmission' is defensible but debatable — this line carries raw/associated gas from offshore wellhead platforms (DP4) to an onshore processing complex (Mellitah) rather than finished gas between transmission hubs, which by strict convention reads more like a gathering/feeder trunk; flagging as a soft note rather than a hard concern since GEM classifies comparable large-bore field-to-plant subsea trunks as transmission elsewhere in this batch (e.g. sibling P6716) for consistency, and I don't have a clean basis to call it definitively wrong. ATTRIBUTION caveat: StartLocation is recorded as generic 'Bouri Platform' rather than the more precise 'DP4 Platform' that every source actually names as this segment's origin — not wrong (DP4 is part of the Bouri field), just looser than it could be. SPEC caveat: one secondary Arabic source, attaqa.net (verified, read closely with verbatim quotes), attributes the 8.5km/20km split differently — it says the 8.5km line runs to Sabratha and the 20km line runs on from Sabratha to the onshore station, the reverse of nsenergybusiness's DP3→DP4 (8.5km) / DP4→Sabratha→onshore (20km) mapping that GEM's row split matches. I weight nsenergybusiness (a dedicated projects-tracking profile with granular platform-to-platform detail) over attaqa's looser business-press paraphrase, and 2026 reporting's language ('Bouri field to Sabratha platform... 10-inch, 20km') sides with nsenergybusiness/GEM's mapping, so I'm not escalating this to a hard concern, but flagging the conflict for the record. DUPLICATE check against the roster: P7617 and P6716 share one gem.wiki page and pipeline_name ('DP3–DP4–Sabratha Gas Pipeline') but are genuinely different physical segments (DP3–DP4, 8.5km/14in vs DP4–Sabratha, 20km/10+4in) with distinct, independently-confirmed specs — this is correct multi-segment splitting, not a duplicate/double-count.

fills.researcher_notes: Owner was blank for this row. rivieramm.com (verified) describes Mellitah Oil & Gas as 'a consortium formed by National Oil Corp of Libya and Eni North Africa' — same operator named for the whole Bouri/DP3-DP4-Sabratha system, and matches sibling row P6716's Owner1/Owner2 names for this same wiki page. Deliberately NOT filling Owner1%/Owner2% (would be 50.00%/50.00% by analogy to P6716) — I could not independently verify the 50/50 split in any source I read, including the one P6716 itself cites (rivieramm.com), which names the JV but never states a percentage. Left blank rather than propagate an unverified number.

Capacity was blank. Two independent 2026 sources both give '125 million cubic feet per day' as the design throughput for gas evacuated from the Bouri field via Sabratha to Mellitah — this is a field/system-level design capacity rather than a pipe-specific rated figure, but since this DP4-Sabratha line is the sole evacuation route for that gas, I'm attributing it here at medium (not high) tier to flag that inference. Left as a soft fill rather than omitting, per instructions to deep-fill blanks with a paired verified ref; downgrade or drop at merge if a stricter pipe-only capacity figure is preferred.

Re-check after September 2026 for a likely operating/StartYear1 update.

summary: Existence, fuel, length (20km) and diameter (10in+4in) all independently confirmed (nsenergybusiness matches GEM's exact segment split; corroborated by fresh 2026 reporting); construction status reconfirmed as of 2026-06 with the project ~69% complete and first gas targeted Sept 2026. One real spec error found: recorded start date '2028' (on a dead, mismatched zawya ref) should be corrected to September 2026 per multiple 2026 sources. Filled blank Owner (NOC/Eni, no % — unverifiable) and Capacity (125 MMcf/d, medium tier) fields. No duplicate/existence/classification concern beyond a soft classification caveat (transmission vs. gathering) and a minor attaqa.net segment-mapping conflict, both noted.
